faq.subtitle: Find quick answers to your questions about Actoos Jobs.

questions.q: What is Actoos Jobs?
questions.a: Actoos Jobs is the leading recruitment platform in Mali and West Africa. We connect qualified candidates with local and international companies. You can search for jobs, apply easily, and track your applications. Recruiters can post jobs, manage applications, and schedule interviews, all for free with a premium subscription option.

questions.q: Is registration free?
questions.a: Yes, registration and basic use are completely free for candidates. Companies can also create a free account and post a limited number of jobs. Paid plans are available for advanced features (more jobs, increased visibility, etc.).

questions.q: How do I create an account?
questions.a: Click on 'Register' at the top right of the site. You can choose a Candidate or Company account. Fill in the form with your email and a password, or quickly log in with Google. Your account will be created instantly.

questions.q: How do I apply for a job?
questions.a: Browse jobs from the 'Jobs' page. Click on a job to see the details, then on 'Apply'. If you haven't completed your profile yet, we will invite you to do so to optimize your chances. Once your application is sent, the company is immediately notified.

questions.q: What is the matching score?
questions.a: It's an estimate of the match between your profile and a job. The higher the score, the more your skills, experience, and salary expectations match what the employer is looking for. It helps you identify the most promising jobs for you.

questions.q: Can I save jobs for later?
questions.a: Absolutely. Click the heart at the top right of the job to add it to your favorites. Find them in your dashboard, under 'Saved jobs'.

questions.q: How do job alerts work?
questions.a: From your dashboard, go to 'Job alerts'. Define your criteria (keywords, city, category, minimum salary, frequency). You will receive an email as soon as a matching job is posted.

questions.q: What should I do if I encounter a technical problem?
questions.a: You can contact us via the contact form (Contact page) or report inappropriate content directly from the job. Our team responds quickly.

questions.q: How do I create a company profile?
questions.a: After creating a 'Company' type account, go to your dashboard and click on 'Create my company'. Fill in the requested information (name, industry, description, logo, etc.). Your company will be submitted for validation by our team. Once validated, you can post jobs.

questions.q: Why is my company pending validation?
questions.a: To ensure the quality and reliability of the offers, we manually verify each new company. This usually takes less than 24 hours. You will be notified by email upon validation. In the meantime, you can prepare your jobs as drafts.

questions.q: How many jobs can I post?
questions.a: With the free plan, you can post 1 active job. The Pro and Business plans allow you to post more jobs simultaneously. You can always save unlimited drafts. Check the 'Pricing' page for more details.

questions.q: How do I manage received applications?
questions.a: In your dashboard, go to 'Applications'. You will see all applications sorted by job. You can change the status (viewed, shortlisted, interview, accepted, rejected). The candidate will be automatically notified by email.

questions.q: Can I schedule a video interview directly from the platform?
questions.a: Yes, on the application detail page, you can generate a Jitsi video conference link in one click and send it by email to the candidate. You can also use our AI assistant to prepare personalized interview questions.

questions.q: How do I cancel my paid subscription?
questions.a: Go to your dashboard, in the subscription section, click on 'Cancel'. You can indicate the reason (optional). Your subscription will be immediately downgraded to the free plan. You will no longer be billed.

questions.q: What payment methods are accepted?
questions.a: We accept credit cards (Visa, Mastercard) via our partner Stripe. All payments are secure and in FCFA (XOF).

questions.q: Can I change plans at any time?
questions.a: Yes, you can upgrade or downgrade. The difference will be calculated pro-rata. Annual plans offer a 20% discount.

questions.q: What happens after a cancellation?
questions.a: Your account remains active and your posted jobs remain online until they expire. You switch back to the free plan and lose access to premium features (additional jobs, boosts, etc.).

questions.q: Is my personal data protected?
questions.a: Yes. We enforce a strict privacy policy. Your information is never shared without your consent. See our 'Privacy' page for more details.

questions.q: How do I report a fraudulent job or abuse?
questions.a: On every job and every company page, you will find a 'Report' button. Select the reason and describe the problem. Our moderation team reviews each report as quickly as possible.

questions.q: Can I delete my account?
questions.a: Yes, contact us via the contact form indicating your request. We will proceed to delete your account and all associated data in accordance with the regulations.

items.title: The 5 trends redefining recruitment in 2026
items.excerpt: Artificial intelligence, hybrid recruitment, soft skills… Discover the major trends transforming the job market this year.
items.content:
Recruitment is changing, and fast

The world of work is evolving at an unprecedented pace. Between the rise of remote work, the automation of HR tasks and the massive arrival of artificial intelligence, recruiters must adapt their methods to attract the best talent.

Here are the 5 major trends shaping recruitment in 2026.

1. AI at the heart of the process

Artificial intelligence no longer just sorts CVs. It writes job descriptions, analyzes soft skills through simulated role-playing and predicts cultural compatibility between a candidate and a company. Recruiters who master these tools gain a decisive competitive advantage.

2. The hybrid model becomes the norm

In 2026, over 60% of job offers provide some form of flexibility. Companies that impose a return to the office 5 days a week struggle to recruit. Remote work is no longer a perk, it's a standard.

3. Soft skills take precedence over degrees

Adaptability, communication, resilience… Recruiters increasingly value human skills. Many companies are removing degree requirements from their offers to focus on real abilities.

4. Employer brand, the #1 lever

Candidates consult an average of 7 sources before applying. A company that takes care of its online presence (employee reviews, social networks, career site) attracts 3 times more qualified applications.

5. Data-driven recruitment

HR dashboards make it possible to measure average recruitment time, cost per hire, and the source of the best candidates. Decisions are no longer made on instinct, but on the basis of concrete data.

Conclusion

The recruitment of tomorrow is already here. Companies that adopt these trends today position themselves as leaders in their sector. And you, are you ready?
items.author: Actoos Team

items.title: Salary negotiation: the complete guide to getting the pay you deserve
items.excerpt: Learn how to prepare your salary negotiation with solid arguments and proven techniques.
items.content:
Why salary negotiation is crucial

According to studies, nearly 60% of candidates accept an offer without negotiating. Yet a successful first negotiation can increase your salary by 10 to 20%. Over an entire career, this represents a considerable difference.

1. Do your research beforehand

Before any interview, find out about salary ranges for your position, your sector and your level of experience. Use specialized platforms, consult annual compensation reports and talk to your network.

2. Identify your added value

List your concrete and quantifiable achievements: revenue growth, cost reduction, successful projects… The more precise your arguments, the stronger your position.

3. Choose the right moment

Don't talk about salary at the first interview. Wait until the company shows a clear interest in your profile. The ideal time is usually after the job offer, when you have demonstrated your value.

4. Adopt the right posture

Stay professional and collaborative. Use phrases like "I'm very enthusiastic about joining your team. Based on my experience and the market, I would aim for a range of…" rather than an aggressive stance.

5. Consider the overall package

The negotiation is not only about base salary. Bonuses, vacation days, remote work, training… All these elements can be negotiated to improve your quality of life.

Conclusion

Negotiating is a right, not a privilege. Prepare yourself, stay professional and don't be afraid to ask for what you're worth. Recruiters respect candidates who know how to defend their interests.
items.author: Actoos Team

items.title: How to create a CV that really stands out in 2026
items.excerpt: The rules of the CV have changed. Clean design, relevant keywords, storytelling… Here's how to grab recruiters' attention in seconds.
items.content:
The CV in 2026: what has changed

A recruiter spends an average of 6 to 10 seconds on a CV before deciding to read it in detail. Your document must therefore be immediately impactful. No more walls of text and cluttered designs: make way for clarity and impact.

1. Opt for a clean and modern design

Use an airy layout, a legible font and clearly defined sections. Modern templates favor sober colors and discreet icons. Avoid tables and overly complex columns that confuse ATS software.

2. Take care of your title and headline

At the top of your CV, a clear title (e.g. "Senior Full Stack Developer") followed by a 2-3 line tagline summarizing your added value allows the recruiter to immediately understand who you are.

3. Quantify your achievements

Replace "Team management" with "Management of an 8-person team, increasing productivity by 25% in 12 months". Numbers speak louder than words.

4. Integrate the right keywords

Analyze the job offers that interest you and identify recurring skills. Integrate them naturally into your CV. This will help you pass recruiters' automatic filters.

5. Add a personal touch

A well-thought-out "Interests" section can make the difference. It humanizes your profile and can create a connection with the recruiter. Mention authentic passions and possibly personal achievements.

Conclusion

A successful CV is one that tells a story and makes people want to know more. Apply these tips and you will significantly increase your chances of getting an interview.
items.author: Actoos Team

items.title: Developing your professional network: strategies that work
items.excerpt: Networking is a long-term investment. Discover how to build and maintain a solid network, even online.
items.content:
Why your network is your best asset

It is estimated that 70 to 80% of job offers are never published. They circulate via the internal network, recommendations and word of mouth. A strong professional network is therefore the key to accessing the hidden job market.

1. Start with your close circle

Former colleagues, classmates, managers… Contact them regularly, not just when you're looking for a job. A simple message to catch up is enough to maintain the relationship.

2. Be active on professional social networks

Publish relevant content, comment on publications in your sector, congratulate your contacts on their successes. Visibility attracts opportunities.

3. Participate in events

Conferences, meetups, webinars… These events are goldmines for expanding your network. Prepare your introduction pitch and don't hesitate to strike up a conversation.

4. Give before you ask

Networking is not a transaction. Share interesting articles, recommend a good service provider, connect two contacts who could collaborate. Your generosity will be noticed.

5. Use a tracking tool

A simple file or a CRM application allows you to note where you stand with each contact. Follow up with people you haven't seen in 6 months, send a message on key dates (work anniversary, new publication).

Conclusion

Your professional network is a marathon, not a sprint. Cultivate it with authenticity and regularity, and it will repay you a hundredfold throughout your career.
items.author: Actoos Team

items.title: Career change: where to start and how to succeed
items.excerpt: Changing careers is a courageous decision. Here are the steps to successfully navigate your transition with peace of mind.
items.content:
You're not alone

A person changes career an average of 5 to 7 times in their working life. Career change is no longer an exception, it's a normal evolution. Here's how to approach it calmly.

1. Do a skills assessment

Before you start, identify your strengths, passions and values. What truly motivates you? In what environment do you thrive? A structured assessment will help you target the professions that suit you.

2. Explore the market

Find out about sectors that are hiring, the skills in demand and available training. Use job platforms, sector reports and testimonials from professionals in the field.

3. Test before you commit

Internships, volunteering, personal projects or job shadowing are excellent ways to discover a profession without risk. This will allow you to confirm your interest and gain initial experience.

4. Train intelligently

Many short, certifying training courses exist, often financeable through public schemes. Prioritize training that leads to concrete skills sought by employers.

5. Adapt your pitch

During interviews, present your career change as an asset. Your atypical background brings a unique perspective, adaptability and unwavering motivation. Recruiters are increasingly sensitive to this.

Conclusion

Career change is a demanding but deeply rewarding path. With good preparation and perseverance, you can give your career a new lease on life.
items.author: Actoos Team

items.title: The 10 fatal job interview mistakes (and how to avoid them)
items.excerpt: Poor preparation, lateness, criticizing a former employer… Discover the traps to absolutely avoid at your next interview.
items.content:
The interview is decided before you even enter the room

A successful interview requires upfront preparation. Unfortunately, many candidates still make mistakes that cost them the job. Here are the 10 most common, and most importantly, how to avoid them.

1. Showing up without knowing the company

A recruiter expects you to have consulted the website, social networks and recent news about the company. Show that you've done your homework by asking relevant questions.

2. Being late

Punctuality is a sign of respect and professionalism. Plan ahead: arrive 10-15 minutes early. If something unforeseen happens, notify them immediately.

3. Criticizing your former employer

Even if your previous experience ended badly, stay neutral and professional. Criticize your former employer and you'll give the impression of being difficult to manage.

4. Reciting your CV

The recruiter has already read your CV. They expect you to elaborate, give concrete examples and show your personality. Don't repeat what's already written.

5. Not asking questions

A candidate with no questions appears to lack interest. Prepare 3 to 5 relevant questions about the position, the team, ongoing projects or the company culture.

6. Lying about your skills

It can seem tempting, but lies always come to light. Be honest about your level, while highlighting your ability to learn quickly.

7. Only talking about salary

The question of compensation is legitimate, but it must come at the right time. Focus first on the value you can bring to the company.

8. Lacking confidence (or being overconfident)

Find the right balance. Neither arrogance nor self-effacement. Prepare examples of your successes and express them with humility and assurance.

9. Forgetting body language

Your posture, your gaze and your handshake say a lot. Maintain eye contact, stand up straight and smile naturally.

10. Not sending a thank you message

A thank you email after the interview shows your professionalism and motivation. It can make the difference between two equivalent candidates.

Conclusion

By avoiding these classic mistakes, you give yourself every chance. Prepare thoroughly and be yourself: that's the best strategy.

cookies.contactText: You can contact us at any time with any questions about our cookie policy: {{email}}

whatIsCookie.title: 1. What is a cookie?
whatIsCookie.content: A cookie is a small text file placed on your device (computer, tablet, mobile) when you browse a website. It stores information about your navigation and improves your user experience. Cookies do not contain viruses and do not allow access to unauthorized personal information.

subsections.title: Strictly necessary cookies
subsections.content:
These are essential for the proper functioning of the site. Without them, certain features (login, security, cart) could not be provided. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable data.

Examples: session cookie, consent preference cookie.

subsections.title: Performance and analytics cookies
subsections.content:
They help us understand how users interact with the site by collecting anonymous data about pages visited, time spent, possible errors. These cookies allow us to continuously improve our services.

We use Google Analytics with IP anonymization.

subsections.title: Functionality cookies
subsections.content:
They allow us to remember your preferences (language, country, currency, login details) to personalize your experience. The site installs them only if you have chosen these options.

Examples: language cookie, country cookie, currency cookie.

subsections.title: Targeting and advertising cookies
subsections.content: Currently, Actoos does not use third-party advertising cookies. If this were to change, you would be informed and explicit consent would be requested before any activation.

thirdParty.title: 3. Third-party cookies
thirdParty.content: Some services we use (hosting, audience analysis, embedded videos) may place their own cookies. We have no direct control over these cookies. We invite you to consult the privacy policy of these third-party services to learn more. Currently, only Google Analytics may place third-party cookies.

manageCookies.title: 4. Managing cookies
manageCookies.content:
On your first visit to our site, a banner informs you about the use of cookies and allows you to customize your choices. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking on the 'Cookie settings' link at the bottom of each page, or by using your browser settings (see next section).

Strictly necessary cookies cannot be disabled as they are essential for the site to function.

browserSettings.title: 5. Browser settings
browserSettings.content:
You can also control cookies directly from your browser settings:
• Google Chrome: Settings > Privacy and security > Cookies and other site data.
• Mozilla Firefox: Options > Privacy & Security > Cookies and Site Data.
• Safari: Preferences > Privacy > Cookies and website data.
• Microsoft Edge: Settings > Cookies and site permissions > Cookies and data stored.

Disabling all cookies may cause the site to function incorrectly.

changes.title: 6. Updates to this policy
changes.content: We may modify this cookie policy at any time. Changes take effect as soon as they are published on this page. We encourage you to review it regularly.

contact.title: 7. Contact
contact.content: For any questions or requests for further information about our cookie policy, you can write to us at the following address: {{email}}

privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.subtitle: How we collect, use and protect your personal data.
privacyPolicy.contactText: For any questions about the protection of your data, you can write to us at: {{email}}

sections.title: 1. Introduction
sections.content: This privacy policy describes how Actoos collects, uses and protects the personal information you provide when using our platform. We are committed to complying with current regulations, including the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable data protection laws.

sections.title: 2. Data collected
sections.content:
We collect the following data:
• Identification data: first name, last name, email address, phone number (optional).
• Professional data: CV, cover letters, experience, skills.
• Browsing data: IP address, pages viewed, visit duration.

This data is collected when you create your account, submit an application or job offer, or simply browse the site.

sections.title: 3. Use of data
sections.content:
Your data is used to:
• Enable the proper functioning of the service (account creation, job posting, connecting recruiters and candidates).
• Improve user experience (browsing analysis, content personalization).
• Send service-related communications (job alerts, newsletters) if you have consented.
• Meet our legal obligations.

sections.title: 4. Data sharing
sections.content:
Your personal data is strictly confidential and is never sold to third parties. It may be shared with:
• Recruiters, when you apply for an offer (your public CV information is accessible to them).
• Our technical service providers (hosting, email sending) bound by confidentiality agreements.
• Competent authorities, if required by law.

You can modify the visibility of your profile at any time in your settings.

sections.title: 5. Data security
sections.content: We implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect your data against unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure or destruction: encryption of sensitive data, restricted data access by our employees, regular security audits.

sections.title: 6. Data retention
sections.content: Your data is retained for the entire duration of your account. If you delete your account, your data is deleted within a maximum of 30 days, unless legal retention obligations apply (e.g. invoices, contractual proof). CVs and applications are deleted as soon as the associated account is deleted.

sections.title: 7. Your rights
sections.content: In accordance with the GDPR, you have the following rights: • Right of access: obtain a copy of your personal data. • Right of rectification: correct inaccurate or incomplete data. • Right to erasure: request deletion of your data (within legal limits). • Right to object: refuse the processing of your data on legitimate grounds. • Right to portability: receive your data in a structured format. To exercise these rights, contact us at {{email}}.

sections.title: 8. Cookies
sections.content: The site uses cookies to improve browsing and analyze traffic. You can manage your preferences at any time via the cookie banner. Cookies strictly necessary for the site to function cannot be disabled.

sections.title: 9. Changes to the policy
sections.content: We reserve the right to modify this privacy policy at any time. Users will be informed of major changes by email or via a notification on the site. We invite you to consult this page regularly.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Actoos, simply.

questions.q: What is Actoos?
questions.a: Actoos is an online recruitment platform that connects companies and candidates internationally. We simplify job searches and job postings, regardless of the country or region.

questions.q: Is registration free?
questions.a: Yes, registration as a candidate or company is completely free. Paid options (Pro, Business) are available for companies that want more features.

questions.q: Who can use Actoos?
questions.a: Anyone looking for a job or any company/recruiter wishing to hire. The platform is multilingual and accessible worldwide.

questions.q: How do I apply for a job?
questions.a: Create a candidate account, complete your profile and upload your CV. You can then apply to the offers that interest you with a single click.

questions.q: Is my profile visible to all companies?
questions.a: You are in control: your profile can be public (visible to recruiters) or private (visible only when you apply). Manage this in your privacy settings.

questions.q: How can I improve my chances of being hired?
questions.a: Complete your profile 100%, add a professional photo, detail your experiences and skills, and personalize your cover letters.

questions.q: How do I post a job offer?
questions.a: Create a company account, get your identity verified, then use the posting form. Your offer will be visible to thousands of candidates.

questions.q: How much does posting cost?
questions.a: The Free plan offers a first posting. The Pro and Business plans give access to more simultaneous offers, boosts and increased visibility. Check the Pricing page for details.

questions.q: Can I manage multiple companies with a single account?
questions.a: Yes, you can create or join several companies and switch between them from your dashboard.

questions.q: What payment methods are accepted?
questions.a: We accept credit cards (Visa, Mastercard) via a secure payment partner. Prices are generally displayed in CFA Francs (XOF) or your local currency.

questions.q: How do I cancel my subscription?
questions.a: You can cancel your subscription at any time from your dashboard, in the Subscription section. The cancellation takes effect at the end of the current period.

questions.q: Can I change plans (monthly → annual)?
questions.a: Yes, you can upgrade, downgrade or change your billing cycle at any time. Price adjustments are calculated automatically.

questions.q: How do I contact support?
questions.a: Write to us at contact@actoos.com or use the contact form on the site. We respond within 24 business hours.

questions.q: I forgot my password. What should I do?
questions.a: Click on 'Forgot password' from the login page. You will receive an email to reset it.

questions.q: How do I report a problem or a fraudulent offer?
questions.a: Use the report button (flag) on each offer or profile. Our moderation team reviews all reports promptly.
